rows.verified: An airspace infringement is unauthorised entry into notified airspace.
Notified airspace includes controlled, prohibited, restricted and active special-use airspace, aerodrome traffic zones, RMZs and TMZs.
Around 1,100 airspace infringements are reported to the CAA each year from the UK and other parts of Europe.
Every infringement has the potential to create a significant safety risk.
All infringements should be reported and reviewed regardless of their apparent immediate effect.
CAA investigations establish facts, identify lessons and consider actions to prevent recurrence.
Around 99% of incidents are processed through the CAP1404 review and actions process.
CAA prevention training covers airspace structures, pre-flight planning, NOTAMs, radiotelephony, transponders, moving maps and recovery from an infringement.
Airspace-infringement risk depends on route planning, airspace complexity, weather, altimetry, radio use, workload and aircraft equipment.
CAA infringement evidence is event-, pilot-, airspace-, aircraft- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level aviation-incident probability.
Drivers are responsible for making sure buses, coaches and other PSVs are safe to drive.
A walkaround check should be completed before the journey.
Defects found before or during the journey must be reported in writing.
Police and DVSA officers may prohibit driving until defects are fixed or issue a fine.
The driver's-seat check includes mirrors, cameras, glass, visibility, wipers, warning lamps, steering and brakes.
Interior checks include doors, emergency exits, accessibility equipment, seats, ventilation and passenger communication systems.
Required emergency equipment such as fire extinguishers and applicable first-aid kits must be present, accessible and serviceable.
Daily records should identify the vehicle, date, defects, reporter and recipient, including a nil-defect entry when no defects are found.
PSV safety risk depends on vehicle design, condition, defect severity, route, passengers, maintenance and driver competence.
PSV walkaround evidence is vehicle-, defect-, operator-, journey- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
